analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/sandboxes.md (head lines 21-23, 30-43, 65-74, 155-166, 214) and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (new 'The cluster waitlist' section, head lines 49-75). No source code, protocol, key handling, attestation, encryption or authorization logic changes. The docs describe a per-account waitlist gate for `darkbloom sandbox setup` (TB-013/T-061) and `darkbloom cluster` (TB-014/T-062). Both docs say the waitlist command sends nothing about the Mac and only puts the account on the list. The sandbox docs still say setup never passes the installer's `--force` and that nothing installs before the user answers y, so the TB-013 and TB-014 confirmation controls are not weakened by the text. The two-mac-cluster text states that already-paired Macs are never asked about the waitlist and that `cluster local` needs no approval; this describes a client-side UX gate, not a trust boundary, and nothing in it claims serving authorization (T-052/T-053) comes from the waitlist. The unit 1e3d03755720606b:0 had no text, only metadata (modified, mode unchanged); the patch and base units cover the content. Open question for integration: the waitlist's actual enforcement (client check versus platform-owned backend) is outside the supplied evidence. The docs reference cli-reference.md anchors that were not supplied. If the check is only client-side, the threat model should not treat it as an access control. This is unverified and not a finding.
